## Overview

The Mass General for Children Pediatric Intensive Care Unit (PICU) is a **14-bed, multidisciplinary unit** that has distinguished itself by providing high-quality care for critically ill infants, children, and adolescents. Our patients present with a wide variety of life-threatening issues, such as severe infections, respiratory diseases, trauma, and post-operative care of various complex surgeries.

Our mission is to provide state-of-the-art critical care medicine by bringing together the most sophisticated technology and scientific advancement in an environment sensitive to the multicultural patients and families we serve. Excellent communication with the family and primary care pediatrician is seen as a critical success factor in optimizing outcomes.

content.caption: Welcome to the Pediatric Intensive Care Unit — Mass General Brigham for Children

content.markdown:
## A coordinated multidisciplinary approach

The Mass General Brigham for Children PICU provides monitoring and life-sustaining treatment for critically ill patients suffering from a wide range of illnesses. We provide advanced cardiovascular, respiratory, and neurological support — both invasive and non-invasive — including **extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO)**.

The PICU attendings are all trained in pediatric critical care medicine. In order to optimize the care of both the child and family, the pediatric intensivists, in collaboration with the critical care nurses, orchestrate a multidisciplinary team that includes medical and surgical physicians, as well as:

- Respiratory therapists
- Pediatric pharmacists
- Physical therapists
- Occupational therapists
- Child life specialists
- Social workers
- Chaplains
- Nutritionists
- Imaging and laboratory personnel

We have a complete range of pediatric consultant services, including:

- Pulmonology
- Endocrinology
- Cardiology and cardiac surgery
- Gastroenterology
- Hematology / oncology
- Infectious diseases
- Neurology
- Nephrology
- Trauma surgery
- General surgery
- Orthopaedic surgery
- Neurosurgery
- Transplant surgery
- Pediatric urology

The PICU fellowship program provides graduate-level patient supervision 24 hours a day.

At Mass General for Children, we strive to provide an open and welcoming environment. We believe that no one knows a child as well as parents do, and therefore parents — along with primary care providers — become **partners in the child's care**. Parents have an active voice in all treatment plans.

## A program of constant improvement

Our procedures and formulary are continually assessed through tools such as the Collaborative Practice Meeting, where novel therapies are evaluated and PICU performance is monitored. Quality assurance is provided through case studies and other forums. Scheduled educational activities are held in the PICU and, by arrangement, in the community.

### Service for sedation and pain-free procedures

The procedural sedation program provides analgesia and/or sedation as appropriate for children in need of potentially painful or anxiety-provoking procedures. This service is provided in a specially decorated, child-friendly patient room within the PICU, which is less intimidating than the operating room. Common procedures include lumbar punctures, bone marrow biopsies, kidney biopsies, central venous catheter placement, and knee taps.

### The TeleHealth program

The Pediatric TeleHealth program provides live video conferencing between the PICU and select patient rooms in emergency departments at outlying community hospitals — including MassGeneral for Children at Salem Hospital, Newton-Wellesley Hospital, and Nantucket Cottage Hospital. Through this link, the PICU staff may provide on-demand medical advice and guidance to help assess, and if needed, stabilize critically ill infants and children and prepare them for transport to the PICU. This telemedicine technology also supports an international link between the Buen Samaritano Hospital in Aguadilla, Puerto Rico and the PICU.

## Research

The Division of Pediatric Critical Care Medicine is performing laboratory and clinical research, including:

- Mechanisms of inflammation, apoptosis, and neuroprotection in brain injury
- Predictors of severity and outcome in severe, acute, and chronic pulmonary diseases
- Applications of innovative technology in the PICU environment

en.description: What to expect in MGfC's Pediatric Emergency Department — facilities, triage, who you'll meet, and FAQ.

content.markdown:
The pediatric emergency department at Mass General Hospital for Children is specially designed from a pediatric perspective to provide exceptional, child-focused care to our patients, as well as support and guidance to their families.

Our larger space is separate from the adult emergency department. It is staffed by physicians, nurses, and other staff trained in pediatric emergency medicine who provide high-quality and developmentally-appropriate care for your child, while ensuring you are involved every step of the way.

## Child- and family-friendly features

The pediatric emergency department has special features to help make your child's visit as smooth and stress-free as possible:

- Six private, child-friendly rooms, including one room specifically designed for suspected or diagnosed infectious disease
- Exam rooms that can accommodate a child and family members if both need emergency care at the same time
- An evaluation area for minor ailments so we can care for patients more efficiently
- A colorful waiting area with tablets and age-appropriate toys
- Interactive LED lights above every bed to help soothe patients while they receive care
- Televisions and DVD controls in every room

> **Your child's comfort and symptoms are very important to us.** Our first priority is to care for patients whose lives are at risk. If you've been to another hospital, that hospital has contacted us — so we are expecting you and your child. We work as quickly as we can to safely care for all patients and to shorten your waiting time.

## Expert services and facilities

The pediatric emergency department provides a full breadth of services and resources, including:

- Access to world-class resources at Massachusetts General Hospital and Mass General Hospital for Children, including pediatric surgery and intensive care units
- **Child Life Specialists** who help your child and family navigate the hospital experience through play and age-appropriate education about treatments, procedures, or exams
- On-site radiology and fluoroscopy (X-rays on video) that deliver low doses of radiation adjusted for your child's age
- 24-hour psychiatric coverage
- Option for conscious sedation (when medically appropriate) to help relieve pain and relax your child

The pediatric emergency department is verified by the American College of Surgeons as a **Level 1 Pediatric Trauma Center** and a **Level 1 Pediatric Burn Center** — the highest trauma center designation. Each year, we treat more than 14,000 children.

## Our triage system

When you arrive, a triage nurse reviews your child's symptoms, medical history, and vital signs. The triage nurse then determines when your child can be seen by one of our doctors trained in pediatric emergency medicine. Depending on the nature of a child's condition or symptoms, they might not always be seen in the order of their arrival:

- **If your child has a life-threatening condition,** they will be evaluated right away.
- **If your child's condition is not life-threatening,** they will be evaluated as soon as possible.

## Frequently asked questions

**Who will be caring for my child?**

There will be many staff members on your child's care team — including registered nurses and doctors trained in pediatric emergency medicine. Your child might also see a nurse practitioner, a medical assistant, or a Child Life specialist from John Hancock Child Life and Wellness Services at MGHfC. Registration staff will also ask you for information while you and your child are in the screening area. They might ask you for detailed information about your child's primary care physician or your health insurance.

**Why am I being asked the same questions over and over again?**

We ask you the same questions to make sure your child receives the most appropriate evaluation possible, and to make sure you and your child stay safe. Initial registration is directed toward getting your child into the system as soon as possible. We might ask you for more information about your child later.

**Can my child have visitors?**

Yes. Please have visitors check in at the information desk to get a visitor's pass.

**Will I be charged for this visit?**

We see all patients whether they can pay or not. If you have insurance, please understand that every plan is different. Co-pays or charges are determined by your individual health plan. Contact your insurance provider if you have other questions.

**Where can I validate my parking?**

Patients and visitors will receive discounted parking without validation. Please show your discharge papers or visitor's pass to the parking attendants.

**Can I use my cell phone?**

Yes, in most areas. Please be sensitive to other patients and staff when making calls. We also have landline phones if you need to use them.

en.description: Tips for your stay in the PICU — visiting hours, medical rounds, the family lounge, sleep rooms, food, parking, and more.

content.markdown:
We would like to partner with you to ensure a safe and comfortable healing environment for all our children and families. Here are some tips for your stay in the Pediatric Intensive Care Unit.

## Visiting

- **Visiting hours:** 11:00 am – 8:00 pm
- For the safety and comfort of all our patients, we are able to accommodate **one parent or guardian per patient overnight**
- Please limit the number of visitors at the bedside to **2 people**
- Siblings are welcome to visit. For the safety of all our patients, siblings may not be left unattended and may not stay overnight.
- Visitors (including siblings) who are sick are asked to please stay home until their symptoms resolve.

## Medical Rounds

Each morning the PICU team will gather outside of your child's room to review information and make a plan of care for the day. **You are invited to participate in rounds.**

After rounding on all of the patients, your doctors will be available to review your child's care plan and answer questions.

## Family Lounge

You are welcome to use the Family Lounge, located around the corner from the Bigelow elevators outside the PICU. It includes:

- A sink, refrigerator, microwave, and coffee
- A table and chairs where you can eat and relax
- A community bathroom with a shower that is wheelchair accessible

Please ask your child's nurse for a towel if needed.

## Where can I sleep?

Sleep rooms are available on a nightly basis. These rooms are given out based on availability and patient condition.

- If you are given a sleep room, please remove your belongings **by 10 am the next day**
- If you need a sleep room for another night, please speak with the Unit Coordinator at the front desk

## Where can I wash my clothes?

There is a washer and dryer located on the inpatient pediatric floor, **Ellison 17**. Turn right when you leave the PICU, follow the signs to the Ellison elevators, and take them to floor 17. Laundry detergent can be provided upon request.

## What food is available?

MGH offers a wide variety of food to purchase in the cafeteria. Take the Bigelow elevators down to the basement (level "B") and follow the signs to **Eat Street Café**.

You may also order a tray of food to be brought to your child's room, but there is a cost associated. If you have financial concerns, please talk to your child's nurse to request social work.

## What activities can my child have?

You are always welcome to bring any comfort items or toys from home. We also have toys, comfort items, and art supplies that can be provided to your child by our staff to help them during their stay. Request the **child life specialist** for more information.

## How can I validate parking?

To receive discounted parking, present your **PICU visitor sticker** to the attendant in the parking garage or in the Yawkey main lobby. Questions related to parking can be directed to the information desk or to your child's nurse.

---

*For more information, please speak with your child's nurse or the Unit Coordinator at the front desk.*

zh-Hant.description: 兒童加護病房入住提示 — 探視時間、醫療查房、家庭休息室、臥室、餐飲、停車等。

content.markdown:
我們願意與您合作,確保為我們所有的兒童和家庭提供安全舒適的治療環境。以下是您在兒童加護病房 (PICU) 入住時的一些提示。

## 訪客

- **探視時間:** 上午 11:00 – 晚上 8:00
- 為了所有患者的安全與舒適,我們能夠為每位患者安排**一位家長或監護人過夜**
- 請將床邊的訪客數量限制在 **2 人**
- 歡迎兄弟姊妹來訪。為了所有患者的安全,兄弟姊妹不得無人看管,也不得過夜
- 生病的訪客(包括兄弟姊妹)需要待在家裡,直到症狀消失為止

## 醫療查房

每天早上,PICU 團隊都會聚集在孩子的病房外,審查資訊並制定當天的照護計畫。**我們邀請您參加查房。**

在對所有患者查完房之後,您的醫生將可審查您孩子的照護計畫並回答問題。

## 家庭休息室

歡迎您使用位於 PICU 外 Bigelow 電梯附近的家庭休息室。這裡設有:

- 水槽、冰箱、微波爐與咖啡
- 桌子和椅子,您可以在那裡就餐和放鬆
- 帶淋浴間的公共盥洗室,輪椅可以使用

如果需要,請向孩子的護士要一條毛巾。

## 我在哪裡睡覺?

每晚都提供臥室。這些房間是根據可用性與患者情況分配的。

- 如果您分到臥室,請於**第二天早上 10 點之前**搬走您的物品
- 如果您需要再一個晚上的臥室,請諮詢前台的房間協調員

## 我在哪裡洗衣服?

**Ellison 17** 住院兒科樓層設有洗衣機和烘乾機。離開 PICU 後向右轉,按照指示牌到達 Ellison 電梯並前往 17 樓。洗衣清潔劑可應要求提供。

## 我可獲取什麼食物?

MGH 提供各種各樣的食物,可在自助餐廳購買。乘坐 Bigelow 電梯到地下層 (「B」層),然後按照指示牌前往 **Eat Street Café**。

您也可以在孩子的房間點一盤食物送到病房,但這是需要付費的。如果您有財務問題,請諮詢您的護士以請求社會工作。

## 我的孩子可以參加什麼活動?

歡迎您從家中帶來任何舒適的物品或玩具。我們也有玩具、舒適物品以及美術用品,可由我們的工作人員為您的孩子提供,以在他們住院期間帶來幫助。向**兒童生活專家**諮詢更多資訊。

## 如何驗證停車?

若要獲得折扣停車,請在停車場或 Yawkey 主大廳向管理員出示 **PICU 訪客貼紙**。有關停車的問題可以直接諮詢詢問台或您孩子的護士。

---

*如需瞭解更多資訊,請諮詢您孩子的護士或前台的房間協調員。*

es.description: Consejos para su estadía en la PICU — horario de visitas, visita del equipo médico, sala familiar, habitaciones para dormir, comida y estacionamiento.

content.markdown:
Quisiéramos colaborar con usted para garantizar un entorno de recuperación seguro y cómodo para todos nuestros niños y familias. Aquí tiene algunos consejos para su estadía en la Unidad de Cuidados Intensivos Pediátricos (PICU, por sus siglas en inglés).

## Visitantes

- **Horario de visitas:** 11:00 am – 8:00 pm
- Por la seguridad y comodidad de todos nuestros pacientes, solo podemos hospedar a **un padre, madre o tutor por paciente durante la noche**
- Por favor, mantenga un límite de **2 visitantes** en la habitación
- Le invitamos a los hermanos a hacer visitas. Por la seguridad de todos nuestros pacientes, los hermanos no pueden pasar la noche ni estar sin supervisión en la unidad.
- Le pedimos encarecidamente a todo visitante que esté enfermo — incluidos los hermanos — que permanezca en casa hasta que se hayan resuelto sus síntomas.

## Visita del equipo médico

Cada mañana, el equipo de la PICU se reunirá fuera de la habitación de su hijo para revisar su información y hacer un plan de atención para el día. **Le invitamos a participar en estas visitas.**

Después de hacerles la visita a todos los pacientes, los médicos de su hijo estarán disponibles para revisar con usted el plan de atención y responder sus preguntas.

## Sala familiar

Le invitamos a usar la sala familiar, ubicada fuera de la PICU al lado de los ascensores de Bigelow. La sala cuenta con:

- Lavamanos, refrigerador, microondas y café
- Una mesa y sillas donde puede comer y relajarse
- Un baño compartido con ducha accesible para sillas de ruedas

Puede pedirle una toalla a la enfermera de su hijo si la necesita.

## ¿Dónde puedo dormir?

Las habitaciones para dormir están disponibles en la noche. El uso de estas habitaciones está sujeto a disponibilidad y a la condición del paciente.

- Si se le proporciona una habitación, por favor retire sus pertenencias **a más tardar a las 10 am del día siguiente**
- Si necesita la habitación para alguna otra noche, por favor hable con el coordinador de la unidad

## ¿Dónde puedo lavar mi ropa?

Hay una lavadora y secadora en el **piso 17 del edificio Ellison**, en la unidad pediátrica de pacientes internados. Al salir de la PICU, gire a la derecha y siga las señales hasta los ascensores de Ellison; suba al piso 17. El detergente está disponible a pedido.

## ¿Hay opciones de comida?

Se vende una amplia variedad de comida en la cafetería del MGH. Tome los ascensores de Bigelow hasta el sótano (oprima "B" en el ascensor) y siga las señales hasta la cafetería **Eat Street Café**.

Puede pedir una bandeja de comida a la habitación de su hijo, pero esto tiene un costo asociado. Si está pasando por dificultades financieras, por favor pídale a la enfermera de su hijo que le ponga en contacto con un trabajador social.

## ¿Qué actividades puede hacer mi hijo?

Usted siempre puede traer de su casa algún juguete u objeto reconfortante o de valor sentimental. Nosotros también tenemos juguetes, objetos reconfortantes y materiales de arte que le podemos proporcionar a su hijo durante su estadía. Para obtener más información, pida una consulta con nuestro **especialista en vida infantil**.

## ¿Cómo obtengo la tarifa de descuento para el estacionamiento?

Para recibir la tarifa de descuento, presente su **vale de visitante de la PICU** al cajero en la planta baja del estacionamiento (garaje) o en el vestíbulo principal del Centro Yawkey. Puede dirigir cualquier pregunta acerca del estacionamiento a la enfermera de su hijo o al personal encargado de los mostradores de información.

---

*Para obtener más información, hable con la enfermera de su hijo o con uno de los coordinadores en la recepción.*

ht.description: Konsèy pou rete nan PICU — orè vizit, vizit medikal, salon familyal, chanm pou dòmi, manje, ak pakin.

content.markdown:
Nou vle travay nan patenarya avèk ou pou asire yon anviwònman gerizon ki sekirize epi ki konfòtab pou tout timoun ak fanmi nou yo. Men kèk konsèy pou rete nan Inite Swen Entansif Pedyatrik (PICU).

## Vizitè

- **Orè vizit:** 11:00 am – 8:00 pm
- Pou sekirite ak konfò tout pasyan nou yo, nou kapab akeyi **yon (1) paran oswa responsab legal pou chak pasyan pandan nuit lan**
- Tanpri, limite kantite vizitè nan chanm pasyan an pou **2 moun**
- Nou ap kontan akeyi frè ak sè yo. Pou sekirite tout pasyan nou yo, nou pa kapab kite frè ak sè yo san siveyans, epi yo pa kapab pase nuit lan nan lopital la.
- Nou ap mande vizitè (san wete frè ak sè) ki malad yo pou rete lakay yo jiskaske sentòm yo a disparèt.

## Vizit medikal

Chak maten, ekip PICU a ap reyini deyò chanm timoun ou an pou revize enfòmasyon yo epi pou etabli yon plan swen pou jounen an. **Nou envite w patisipe nan vizit yo.**

Apre yo fin vizite tout pasyan yo, doktè ou yo ap disponib pou egzamine plan swen timoun ou an epi pou reponn kesyon ou yo.

## Salon familyal

Ou kapab itilize Salon Familyal la ki twouve li nan ang asansè Bigelow yo, deyò PICU a. Li gen:

- Yon evye, yon frijidè, yon mikwo-ond, ak kafe
- Yon tab ak chèz kote ou kapab manje epi detann ou
- Yon saldeben kominotè ki gen douch ki aksesib pou chèz woulant

Tanpri, mande enfimyè timoun ou an yon sèvyèt si sa nesesè.

## Ki kote mwen kapab dòmi?

Gen chanm pou dòmi ki disponib sou baz chak nuit. Nou atribye chanm sa yo selon disponibilite ansanm ak eta sante pasyan an.

- Si ou jwenn yon chanm pou dòmi, tanpri retire bagay pèsonèl ou yo **anvan 10 am nan demen**
- Si ou bezwen yon chanm pou pase yon lòt nuit, tanpri pale sou sa ak Kowòdonatè Inite a ki nan resepsyon an

## Ki kote mwen kapab lave rad mwen?

Gen yon machin a lave ak yon machin pou seche rad nan etaj pasyan ki entène yo, **Ellison 17**. Vire adwat lè ou kite PICU a, suiv pano ki endike asansè Ellison yo, epi monte nan etaj 17 la. Nou kapab bay pwodui netwayaj si ou mande sa.

## Ki manje ki disponib pou mwen?

MGH pwopoze yon pakèt varyete aliman pou achte nan kafeterya a. Pran asansè Bigelow yo rive jis nan etaj anba nèt la ("B"), epi suiv pano ki ekri **Eat Street Café** yo.

Ou kapab kòmande yon plato aliman nan chanm timoun ou an, men gen yon pri pou sa. Si ou gen pwoblèm finansyè, tanpri pale ak enfimyè ou a pou mande èd sosyal.

## Ki aktivite timoun mwen an kapab fè?

Ou kapab toujou vini ak nenpòt atik konfò oswa jwèt li gen lakay li. Epitou, nou gen jwèt, atik konfò, ak materyèl atizay manm pèsonèl nou an kapab bay timoun ou an pou ede li pandan tan li nan lopital la. Pou plis enfòmasyon, pale avèk **espesyalis lavi timoun nan**.

## Kijan mwen kapab valide pakin nan?

Pou w resevwa yon rediksyon sou pakin nan, montre **otokolan vizitè PICU ou a** bay moun ki nan pakin nan oswa ki nan chanm prensipal Yawkey a. Ou kapab poze kesyon ki gen rapò ak pakin yo nan biwo enfòmasyon an oswa bay enfimyè ou a.

---

*Pou plis enfòmasyon, tanpri pale avèk enfimyè timoun ou an oswa Kowòdonatè Inite a ki nan resepsyon an.*

ar.description: نصائح أثناء إقامتك في وحدة العناية المركزة للأطفال — ساعات الزيارة، الجولات الطبية، صالة العائلات، الغرف، الطعام، ووقوف السيارات.

content.markdown:
يسرّنا أن نتشارك سويًا لضمان الاستمتاع ببيئة علاجية آمنة ومريحة لجميع أطفالنا وعائلاتنا. فيما يلي بعض النصائح أثناء إقامتك في وحدة العناية المركزة للأطفال (PICU).

## الزائرون

- **ساعات الزيارة:** 11:00 صباحًا – 8:00 مساءً
- للحفاظ على سلامة مرضانا وراحتهم، يمكن أن يرافق كل مريض طوال فترة الليل **أحد الوالدين أو الوصي**
- يُرجى أن يقتصر عدد الزائرين في الغرفة على **شخصين**
- يسرّنا استقبال الأخوة. للحفاظ على سلامة جميع مرضانا، يحظر ترك الأخوة دون مراقبة وغير مسموح ببقائهم طوال فترة الليل.
- يُطلب من الزائرين، بما في ذلك الأخوة، المرضى البقاء في المنزل حتى زوال أعراضهم.

## الجولات الطبية

سيجتمع فريق وحدة العناية المركزة للأطفال معًا كل صباح خارج الغرفة التي يقيم فيها طفلك لمراجعة المعلومات ووضع خطة رعاية لهذا اليوم. **أنت مدعو للمشاركة في الجولات.**

بعد المرور في جولات على جميع المرضى، سيكون أطباؤك متاحين لمراجعة خطة رعاية طفلك والإجابة على الاستفسارات التي تساورك.

## صالة العائلات

يمكنك استخدام صالة العائلات التي توجد بالقرب من مصاعد Bigelow خارج وحدة العناية المركزة للأطفال. تشمل:

- مغسلة وثلاجة وميكروويف وماكينة قهوة
- طاولة وكراسي حيث يمكنك الجلوس لتناول الطعام والاسترخاء
- حمام مشترك مع دش ملائم لمستخدمي الكراسي المتحركة

يُرجى أن تطلب من ممرضة طفلك الحصول على منشفة، إذا لزم الأمر.

## أين يمكنني النوم؟

تتوفّر الغرف المخصّصة للنوم ليلًا. يتم توزيع هذه الغرف على أساس التوفّر وحالة المريض.

- إذا تم توفير غرفة نوم لك، فيُرجى إزالة متعلقاتك **بحلول الساعة 10 صباحًا من اليوم التالي**
- إذا كنت بحاجة إلى غرفة نوم لليلة أخرى، فيُرجى التحدث مع منسّق الوحدة في مكتب الاستقبال

## أين يمكنني غسل ملابسي؟

توجد غسالة ومجفف في طابق مرضى عيادات الأطفال الداخلية، الواقعة في **Ellison 17**. انعطف يمينًا بعد الخروج من وحدة العناية المركزة للأطفال واتبع اللافتات المؤدية إلى مصاعد Ellison ثم اصعد إلى الطابق 17. يمكن توفير منظفات الغسيل عند الطلب.

## ما الأطعمة المتاح لي تناولها؟

تقدم MGH مجموعة واسعة من الأطعمة المتوفّرة للشراء في الكافتيريا. استقل مصاعد Bigelow نزولًا إلى الطابق السفلي ("B") واتبع اللافتات المؤدية إلى **Eat Street Café**.

يمكنك أن تطلب توصيل صينية الطعام إلى غرفة طفلك، لكن يتم فرض تكلفة إضافية. إذا كانت لديك مخاوف مالية، فيُرجى التحدث مع ممرضتك لطلب العمل الاجتماعي.

## ما الأنشطة التي يمكن أن يمارسها طفلي؟

يمكنك دائمًا إحضار أي أدوات أو ألعاب ملائمة من المنزل. يتوفّر لدينا أيضًا ألعاب وأدوات ملائمة ولوازم فنية يمكن أن يقدمها العاملون لدينا لطفلك لمساعدتهم أثناء إقامتهم. اطلب من **أخصائي حياة الطفل** الحصول على المزيد من المعلومات.

## كيف يمكنني التحقّق من ساحة الركن المُخصّصة لوقوف السيارات؟

للوقوف في ساحة ركن بسعر مخفض، يمكنك تقديم **ملصق زائر وحدة العناية المركزة للأطفال** الخاص بك إلى الموظف في مرآب السيارات أو ردهة Yawkey الرئيسية. يمكن توجيه الأسئلة المتعلقة بساحات ركن السيارات إلى مكتب المعلومات أو إلى الممرضة المسؤولة عن الحالة الخاصة بك.

---

pt.description: Dicas para sua estadia na UTIP — horário de visitas, rondas médicas, saguão da família, quartos para dormir, alimentos e estacionamento.

content.markdown:
Gostaríamos de fazer parceria com você para assegurar um ambiente de cura seguro e confortável para todas as nossas crianças e famílias. Aqui estão algumas dicas para sua estadia na Unidade de Tratamento Intensivo Pediátrica (UTIP).

## Visitantes

- **Horário de visitas:** 11:00 – 20:00
- Para a segurança e conforto de todos os nossos pacientes, podemos acomodar **um pai, mãe ou responsável por paciente durante a noite**
- Limite o número de visitantes no leito para **duas pessoas**
- Irmãos são bem-vindos para visitar. Para a segurança de todos os nossos pacientes, os irmãos não podem ser deixados sem supervisão e não podem permanecer durante a noite.
- Visitantes (incluindo irmãos) que estão doentes são solicitados a permanecer em casa até que os sintomas desapareçam.

## Rondas médicas

A cada manhã, a equipe da UTIP se reunirá fora do quarto da sua criança para revisar as informações e fazer um plano de tratamento para o dia. **Você está convidado a participar das rondas.**

Após atender todos os pacientes, os médicos estarão disponíveis para revisar o plano de tratamento da sua criança e responder perguntas.

## Saguão da Família

Você é bem-vindo para usar o Saguão da Família, localizado na esquina dos elevadores Bigelow fora da UTIP. Há:

- Uma pia, geladeira, micro-ondas e café
- Uma mesa e cadeiras onde você pode comer e relaxar
- Um banheiro comunitário com chuveiro acessível para cadeira de rodas

Peça para a enfermeira de sua criança uma toalha, se necessário.

## Onde eu posso dormir?

Os quartos para dormir estão disponíveis por noite. Esses quartos são fornecidos com base na disponibilidade e na condição do paciente.

- Se for dado a você um quarto para dormir, remova seus pertences **até as 10h do dia seguinte**
- Se você precisar de um quarto para dormir para uma outra noite, fale com o Coordenador da Unidade na recepção

## Onde eu posso lavar minhas roupas?

Há uma lavadora e secadora no andar pediátrico de internação, **Ellison 17**. Vire à direita quando sair da UTIP, siga as placas para os elevadores Ellison e vá até o 17.° andar. Detergente para roupas pode ser fornecido mediante solicitação.

## Qual alimento está disponível para mim?

O MGH oferece uma ampla variedade de alimentos para comprar na cafeteria. Pegue os elevadores Bigelow até o subsolo ("B") e siga as placas para o **Eat Street Café**.

Você pode pedir uma bandeja de alimentos para ser levada ao quarto da sua criança, mas há um custo associado. Se você tiver preocupações financeiras, fale com sua enfermeira para solicitar um assistente social.

## Quais atividades a minha criança pode ter?

Você é sempre bem-vindo para trazer quaisquer itens de conforto ou brinquedos de casa. Também temos brinquedos, itens de conforto e materiais de arte que podem ser fornecidos para sua criança pela nossa equipe para ajudá-la durante a estadia. Solicite mais informações ao **especialista em vida infantil**.

## Como eu posso validar o estacionamento?

Para receber desconto no estacionamento, apresente seu **adesivo de visitante da UTIP** para o atendente na garagem do estacionamento ou na entrada principal do Yawkey. Perguntas relacionadas ao estacionamento podem ser dirigidas à mesa de informações ou à sua enfermeira.

---

*Para obter mais informações, fale com a enfermeira da sua criança ou com o Coordenador da Unidade na recepção.*

en.description: Child life specialists help children and families cope with hospitalization through play, education, and therapeutic programs.

content.markdown:
## What is the Child Life & Pediatric Integrative Therapies Program?

The Child Life and Pediatric Integrative Therapies Program at Mass General Brigham for Children helps children and adolescents navigate the mental, emotional, and social effects of illness, medical treatment, and hospitalization.

As part of the care team, our **board-certified child life specialists** foster positive coping skills and empower children throughout their healthcare experience.

## Our Services

### Preparation and Education

Our child life specialists provide preparation and education for potentially painful procedures, new or unfamiliar diagnoses, and the nature of the hospital environment. Our team works with patients and families to create a coping plan for procedures using techniques like play, guided imagery, and deep breathing. Child life specialists collaborate with the medical team to provide developmentally appropriate diagnosis education to children to promote understanding.

### Developmental Support

With expertise in child development, child life specialists use play to support typical development — intellectual, motor, emotional, and social skills. Engaging in these activities can support children in reaching developmental milestones.

### Normalization and Play

The hospital can be a scary place for children, with many new sights and sounds. Our child life team works to create a child-friendly environment through welcoming spaces (like activity rooms) and opportunities to engage in medical and therapeutic play, creative expression, and peer socialization.

### Enhancing Coping and Emotional Regulation

Child life specialists work with children and families to increase coping and normalization of the environment. These skills include techniques such as mindfulness, guided imagery, relaxation, and distraction. This is particularly valuable during medical procedures and lengthy admissions.

### Family Involvement and Bonding

Through art, music, and play, our child life team can help promote emotional expression and support children in processing their medical experience. With a passion for advocacy and compassion, child life specialists support families through big challenges. Child life specialists also offer legacy-building opportunities during moments of change and loss.

### Art Therapy and Music Therapy

Our music and art therapists use therapeutic interventions to promote wellness.

- **Music therapy** can help support a child's experience through active music making, gentle live music for relaxation, music-supported meditation, or creating recordings to share with loved ones.
- **Art therapy** can be tailored to a child's interests to raise self-esteem and self-awareness.

With the help of a board-certified music therapist and art therapist, patients can explore how music and art might best support them during a challenging hospital admission.

> Child life and pediatric integrative therapies are designed to **complement, not replace,** conventional medical treatments. Collaborative efforts ensure a well-rounded and supportive approach to pediatric healthcare.

## Special Programming

The child life department collaborates with programming throughout inpatient and outpatient pediatric areas. Current special programming may include:

### Acupuncture and Acupressure

Acupuncture uses fine, sterile needles applied to specific areas of the body to stimulate energy flow; acupressure involves applying gentle pressure to these same points with the hands. The acupuncturist will work with you and your care team.

### Art Therapy Group

A peer space designed to provide pediatric patients with an overall sense of community and reduce feelings of isolation through engagement with the visual arts and supportive conversation — using painting, coloring, drawing, sculpting, and building, alongside applied psychological theory facilitated by a board-certified art therapist.

### Child Life Volunteers

Child Life volunteers support and provide play opportunities for our inpatient population.

### Club STAR

A **bereavement peer support group** for children and teens (kindergarten through senior year of high school) grieving the death of a parent or sibling. The group meets monthly, in person or via Zoom. Dinner and parking are provided for in-person groups. Club STAR is organized by child life specialists from Mass General Brigham for Children.

For more information or to register, please contact Hillary D'Amato, MSW, CCLS:
- 📞 [617-643-9276](tel:+16176439276)
- ✉️ [mghclubstar@partners.org](mailto:mghclubstar@partners.org)

### Facility Dog Kayce

Meet **Kayce**, the first facility dog at Mass General Brigham for Children. He joined the hospital as an employee and member of the Child Life team in September 2024. Kayce is specially trained to help children cope and overcome the stress they may experience during a stay at the hospital.

### Hearts & Noses Hospital Clown Troupe

Hospital clowns specially trained to engage, empower, and give choices to children and adults in a medical environment. Clowns receive extensive professional training in the delicate art of engaging children in the hospital — creating an environment that supports play and puts the child in control of the interaction.

### Healing Little Heroes

A non-profit organization that brings superheroes like Captain America and Spider-Man to the bedside of pediatric patients.

### Hero Circle — Martial Arts Program

Hero Circle teaches martial arts meditation, movement, and breathing techniques designed to empower children to take control of the pain and stress of their illness. Children **3 years and older** with any pediatric illness, and their siblings, may be eligible for the program.

### Hole in the Wall Gang Camp — Hospital Outreach Program (HOP)

HOP brings the magic of The Hole in the Wall Gang Camp for Seriously Ill Children (founded by Paul Newman in 1988) to patients in the hospital by providing camp activities at the bedside. HOP specialists visit many areas of the hospital to engage children in games, arts and crafts, and fun.

### Massage Therapy

Can help relieve stress, increase relaxation, and lead to a feeling of greater well-being. Massage can alleviate some of the physical symptoms and side effects of treatment, and often relieves pain resulting from excess muscle tension.

### Pet Therapy

A visit from a furry, friendly, and specially trained dog with a trained volunteer handler.

---

*Additional special programming may be available within specific units. Programming is subject to change and may not be available on request. Speak with your child life specialist for more information.*

*Thank you to all of our community partners, donors, and organizations that bring joy to the children and families at Mass General Brigham for Children.*

en.description: Understand the different roles of doctors caring for your child — attendings, consultants, fellows, residents, and medical students.

content.markdown:
# Who’s Who on the Medical Team Taking Care of My Child?

Welcome to Mass General Hospital for Children. You and your child's doctors, nurses, social workers, and therapists make up the healthcare team — with **you as the most important member**. The information below will help you understand the different types of doctors on the *Medical Team* that will be involved in your child's care.

## Attending Physician

This is the doctor who **leads the medical team** that plans the care and treatment for your child. They will work closely with you to make decisions about your child's care, and are ultimately responsible for the medical care provided by the team.

Your child's Attending Physician will either be:

- A **Pediatrician who specializes in Hospital Medicine**, called a *Hospitalist*
- A **Subspecialist Pediatrician**, who has a specialty in a certain area of pediatrics (such as a Pediatric Pulmonologist, who specializes in children's lung problems)
- A physician from your child's primary care practice

If you are not sure who your child's Attending Physician is, please ask us.

## Consulting Physician

This is a Pediatrician who has a specialty in a specific area (same as a Subspecialist) and is called in to *consult* on your child's case. This specialist will work with the medical team to diagnose, treat, and care for your child.

They may also work with a **Pediatric Fellow** — a doctor who has completed medical residency training in Pediatrics and is now in training to become a subspecialist (e.g., a Pediatric Pulmonologist).

The Consulting Physician and Fellow will make recommendations to the Attending Physician and resident team.

## Resident Physician (or House Officer)

This is a doctor who has graduated from medical school and is now in a resident training program to become a Pediatrician. A Pediatric resident program usually takes 3 years to complete, and Residents are referred to by the year they are currently in:

- **First-year residents** are also called *Interns*. An intern will examine your child every day and is usually the first person called if you have a question or concern. Your child will have a primary Intern while they are in the hospital.
- **Second-year residents** are in between their first and third year. They don't have any other special name.
- **Third-year residents** are also known as *Senior Residents*. They oversee the work of medical interns and medical students.

Residents work with the Attending Physician to give your child the best care possible. The Pediatric floor at MGH has a Resident Physician available **24 hours a day**.

## Medical Students

Medical students are in the third and fourth year of medical school. **Third-year students** work with Interns to help care for your child. **Fourth-year students** usually work under the Senior Resident to care for your child.

---

Mass General Hospital for Children is committed to providing you with the highest standard of care. We think this is enhanced by being a Harvard teaching hospital.

Sometimes it can be hard to tell who is who in a place bustling with so many pediatric doctors. All members of your child's medical team should introduce themselves and their role on the team.

> **If you are uncertain who a person is, please ask them to introduce themselves.**

## Why choose Mass General Brigham for Children

The Division of Pediatric Hematology and Oncology is a comprehensive children's program backed by the full resources of Massachusetts General Hospital and close collaboration with adult colleagues in the [Mass General Cancer Center](https://www.massgeneral.org/cancer-center). Doctors who specialize in the care of children provide personalized, state-of-the-art care to children of all ages with malignancies and disorders of the blood.

### Pediatric Hematology Program

Specialized expertise in anemias (including sickle cell disease), thrombocytopenia, neutropenia, aplastic anemia and other bone marrow failure syndromes. Expert consultation and management of bleeding and clotting disorders including von Willebrand disease, hemophilia, thrombosis, and stroke.

content.markdown:
### Pediatric Oncology Program

Multidisciplinary, comprehensive, family-centered care for children with all types of cancer. The clinical team has expertise in treating leukemias, lymphomas, common solid tumors of childhood (including Wilms tumor, neuroblastoma, bone and soft tissue sarcomas, retinoblastoma, and brain tumors).

- [Bone and Soft Tissue Program](https://www.massgeneral.org/children/cancer/bone-and-soft-tissue-sarcoma-program)
- [Head and neck tumors](https://www.massgeneral.org/children/cancer/head-and-neck-clinic)
- [Pediatric brain tumors](https://www.massgeneral.org/children/cancer/brain-tumor-clinic)
- [Leukemia](https://www.massgeneral.org/children/cancer/leukemia-clinic) and [lymphoma](https://www.massgeneral.org/children/cancer/lymphoma-clinic)
- [Long-Term Follow-Up Clinic](https://www.massgeneral.org/children/cancer/longterm-followup-clinic)

## Treatment

Mass General Brigham for Children delivers the latest and most advanced treatments for childhood cancers and blood disorders.

- **[Pediatric surgical oncology](https://www.massgeneral.org/children/pediatric-surgery/surgical-oncology):** In addition to open surgery, minimally invasive techniques such as video-assisted thoracoscopy, laparoscopy, and robotic-assisted surgery are available to remove solid tumors.
- **[Pediatric radiation oncology](https://www.massgeneral.org/cancer-center/radiation-oncology/treatments-and-services/pediatric-radiation-oncology):** Home to the only [proton therapy](https://www.massgeneral.org/children/proton-therapy) site in New England. Proton therapy for children can be used to treat pediatric tumors while minimizing long-term effects on growth and development.
- **[Clinical trials](https://www.massgeneral.org/cancer-center/clinical-trials-and-research/search-clinical-trials.page?cancerCondition=Pediatric+Cancers):** Patients receive research-driven cancer treatment through access to the latest clinical trials in cancer and hematology. The Division is a member of the [Children's Oncology Group (COG)](https://childrensoncologygroup.org/) and the [Pediatric Hodgkin Lymphoma Consortium](https://www.stjude.org/care-treatment/treatment/childhood-cancer/leukemia-lymphoma/hodgkin-lymphoma.html) based at St. Jude Children's Hospital.

## Integrated, multidisciplinary care

The patient care team is led by a pediatric hematologist-oncologist. Depending on the type of tumor and treatment plan, other team members may include:

- Surgical specialists (pediatric surgery, thoracic surgery, neurosurgery, urology, otolaryngology, orthopedics, orthopedic oncology, ophthalmology, oculoplastics, plastic surgery)
- Pediatric radiation oncologists (for those considered for proton beam, intensity-modulated, or other radiation therapy)
- Senior-level oncology-certified nurses and nurse practitioners
- Child psychiatrists, social workers, and [child life specialists](https://www.massgeneral.org/children/child-life)
- Nutritionists, physical therapists, and rehabilitation medicine specialists

## Adolescent and Young Adult (AYA) Cancer Program

The [Adolescent and Young Adult Cancer Program](https://www.massgeneral.org/cancer-center/patient-and-family-resources/supportive-care/adolescent-and-young-adult-program) was created to optimize the care, outcomes, and experiences of adolescent and young adult patients.

## Patient resources

For the full collection of patient resources from Pediatric Hematology and Oncology, visit the [Patient Resources page](https://www.massgeneral.org/children/cancer/patient-resources) on massgeneral.org.

content.markdown:
## Contact Information

**Pediatric Supportive & Palliative Care**
Yawkey Center for Outpatient Care
55 Fruit Street, Boston, MA 02114

- 📞 [617-643-9079](tel:+16176439079)
- Fax: 617-724-8896

## Overview

Pediatric Supportive & Palliative Care at Mass General Brigham for Children supports children with chronic, life-threatening, or life-limiting illnesses — and their families — by enhancing their quality of life.

Our team offers support to children with serious conditions and their families anywhere along their illness course, including families facing pregnancies complicated by genetic disorders or congenital malformations. We work with your child's primary and specialist teams to provide the best possible care. Our team aims to:

- **Identify your family's goals and values**
- **Ease distressing symptoms**
- **Optimize quality of life**
- **Improve communication** between care teams and families
- **Help families navigate** the best treatment choices for them and their child

Our team is primarily an inpatient consultative service made up of pediatric palliative care doctors and a pediatric nurse practitioner. We collaborate closely with your child's care providers within Mass General Brigham for Children and in the community — including primary care physicians, subspecialists, nurses, child life specialists, spiritual care providers, and physical, occupational, and speech therapists.

While your child is in the hospital, their medical providers may invite our service to join the care team. In outpatient settings, providers may also consult or refer children to our service.

> If you are interested in seeing if palliative care may benefit your child's treatment, please call our office at 📞 [617-643-9079](tel:+16176439079) and leave a message. We will return your call to determine if, and how, our team may be helpful.

## Programs

### Mass General Brigham for Children Center for Courageous Kids

Our Pediatric Supportive & Palliative Care team, alongside the Coordinated Care Clinic, has received funding to create the **Center for Courageous Kids**. This center provides multidisciplinary, compassionate care for children with complex medical needs and life-limiting illnesses. The aim is to improve quality of life for these children and their families.

### No Empty Bedsides

We are grateful partners with [**No Empty Bedsides**](http://www.noemptybedsides.com/index.html), a volunteer fundraising organization providing financial support to parents and families of hospitalized children cared for by Supportive & Palliative Care.

No Empty Bedsides assists with:

- Public transportation costs
- Parking fees
- Backup care for the hospitalized child's siblings

It helps to ensure that every child has a loved one by their side during a hospital stay.

### Courageous Parents Network

We are proud partners with [**Courageous Parents Network**](https://courageousparentsnetwork.org/), a website designed to support and empower families whose child faces serious illness, and to enlighten caregivers about the lived experience of these families.

## Bereavement resources

### For adults

- **Mass General Bereavement Support Group** — Open to patients and employees of the Mass General community. An 8-week group for people who have experienced the death of a loved one within the past 1½ years. Fee covered by most insurances and Medicare. To refer or to schedule a pre-group screening interview, contact Marie Herbert, MSW, LICSW: 📞 [617-726-8199](tel:+16177268199).
- **[The Compassionate Friends](http://www.compassionatefriends.org/)** — Organization dedicated to assisting families toward positive resolution of grief following the death of a child of any age. Chapters across the U.S. and internationally. 📞 [877-969-0010](tel:+18779690010)
- **[Association of Death Education & Counseling](http://www.adec.org/)** — Online resources for coping with loss; referrals to support groups throughout the U.S. 📞 [847-509-0403](tel:+18475090403)
- **[Hospice Foundation of America](http://www.hospicefoundation.org/)** — Support and education about death, illness, and bereavement. Referrals to grief support groups, monthly bereavement newsletter, and annual "Living with Grief" teleconference series. 📞 [800-854-3402](tel:+18008543402)

### For children and teens

- **Club STAR: Sharing Together and Remembering** — A group for ages 5–18 and their parents grieving the death of a parent or sibling. Meets 5:30 – 7:30 pm on the first Wednesday of October–June at Mass General Hospital. Organized by Mass General for Children, Child Life Services, and the Social Service Department. To register, contact Hillary D'Amato, MS, CCLS: 📞 [617-643-9276](tel:+16176439276) or [mghclubstar@partners.org](mailto:mghclubstar@partners.org).
- **[Jeff's Place](https://www.jeffsplace.org/)** — Free, bi-monthly, open-ended peer support groups for children ages 3–19 and their caregivers coping with the death of a loved one. Individual and small groups in Framingham, MA; large groups in Wayland, MA. 📞 [508-276-3225](tel:+15082763225)
- **[Comfort Zone Camps](http://www.comfortzonecamp.org/)** — Free weekend camps for children ages 7–17 who have experienced the death of a parent, sibling, or primary caregiver. Creates an environment where grieving children can have fun while learning coping skills.
- **[The Dougy Center for Grieving Children & Families](http://www.dougy.org/)** — Headquartered in Portland, Oregon. Their website offers tools for children, teens, and young adults who are grieving. 📞 [866-775-5683](tel:+18667755683)
- **[The Garden: A Center for Grieving Children and Teens](https://www.cooleydickinson.org/programs-services/vna-hospice/the-garden/)** — Based in Northampton, MA. Programs and discussion groups help young people identify and share their feelings. Parents and guardians meet separately. No charge to families. Email [shelly.thegarden@gmail.com](mailto:shelly.thegarden@gmail.com) for information.

> This is not a full list of resources available to you and your family. If you have questions about the resources listed or would like more information about bereavement support, please contact the Mass General Hospital Social Service Department: 📞 [617-726-2643](tel:+16177262643).

title: Support for Siblings of a Special Needs Child

en.description: How siblings react when a brother or sister has special needs — by age — plus parenting tips, warning signs, and Sibshops support.

content.markdown:
Families tell us that managing family life with a special needs child is tough. Parents say that caring for the ill or disabled child takes so much time and energy that they can't always pay as much attention to their other children as they might like. This can make siblings feel neglected — even when mom and dad are doing their best to pay equal attention to everyone.

We hope these tips will help you better understand what happens when a family member requires special care and attention, and give you ideas to help make things easier for everyone in your family.

## Understanding your healthy or typically developing children — by age

### Preschoolers (before age 5)

Young children can't understand what is actually wrong with their sibling, and:

- Can't express their feelings with words and may act them out
- Notice some differences between what their sibling can and can't do, and may try to teach their sibling how to do things

### School-age children (6–12)

Children of this age can understand that their sibling has special needs. However, they may:

- Worry that the disability or illness is catching
- Feel guilty about having negative thoughts and feelings about their sibling
- Become either over-helpful and well-behaved, or badly behaved to get attention
- Have confusing, mixed feelings about their sibling (love, resentment, anger, loyalty)

### Teens (13–17)

Older children can understand explanations of the disability or illness, and may:

- Ask detailed questions of parents
- Be embarrassed in front of friends and dates
- Be torn between their freedom and wanting a special relationship with their sibling
- Resent the amount of responsibility they have for their sibling

## At any age

### Your healthy or typically developing children may feel:

- **Embarrassment** over the way siblings act or look
- **Anger or jealousy** over the amount of attention their siblings get
- **Pressure** to "make up" for a sibling's disability by being perfect at home, in school, or at a sport or music, etc.
- **Guilt** about being healthy

### But they may also develop:

- **Maturity** that is greater than their age
- **Pro-social behaviors** (helping others, kindness, etc.)
- **Understanding** of challenges of others and the advantages most people take for granted
- **Tolerance** for differences
- **Pride** about the disabled sibling's accomplishments
- **Loyalty and caring** towards their sibling

## Parenting tips

- Try to give each child a regularly scheduled special time with each parent alone and together. If you are a single parent, try to give each child regularly scheduled special time with another adult family member or friend who the child is close to.
- When planning family activities, remember that not everything has to be done with the whole family. If an activity is too much for the special needs child, arrange for their care while the family is out.
- Encourage each child to have their own interests, and give each one a special space for personal things.
- Recognize each child's unique strengths and accomplishments, and make sure they develop friendships outside the family.
- Have the special needs child do as much as they can for themselves, and any other chores they are able to do.
- Keep the same rules for the special needs child as the others whenever possible.
- Listen to brothers' and sisters' worries about their disabled sibling.
- Establish and keep daily routines as much as possible.
- And, of course, let all your children know they are loved and valued.

## Things to watch for

These behaviors may mean that your typically developing child could use some more help:

- Unusually aggressive language, fighting words
- Refusing to attend school, or fear of school
- Depression
- Sleep or eating changes
- Lack of interest in things they usually enjoy
- Increased anxiety or worries
- Loss of self-esteem or confidence
- Lowered achievement
- Frequent complaints of not feeling well

> If you see any of these signs, please discuss them with your child's doctor.

## Mass General for Children Sibshops

Mass General for Children runs a support group for siblings of special needs children called **Sibshops**. Sibshops provide opportunities for siblings to get peer support and education in a lively and fun setting. We mix interesting information and discussion with games as well as special guests.

en.description: Six concrete starting points for finding a licensed therapist — insurance, the state help line, matching services, EAP, and more.

content.markdown:
Finding a therapist can be the first step toward learning new ways to handle difficult situations. Look for a **licensed** therapist.

## Licensed psychotherapists include:

- **Clinical Social Workers (LICSW)** — Master's degree in Social Work (MSW) with at least several years of supervised experience.
- **Clinical Psychologists** — Ph.D. in Psychology. May do psychological testing in addition to psychotherapy.
- **Psychiatrists** — Medical doctors who have had additional training in psychiatry. Can prescribe medication.
- **Psychiatric Nurse Clinicians** — Nurses with master's degrees who may provide psychotherapy and prescribe medication.

## Getting started

### 1. Call your insurance company

See your card for contact information. Your insurance may require you to use one of their preferred providers.

### 2. Massachusetts residents — contact the 24/7 Behavioral Health Help Line

Get the treatment or support you need, find a provider, and make an appointment.

- 📞 Call or text [833-773-2445](tel:+18337732445)
- Chat at [masshelpline.com](https://www.masshelpline.com)
- Helps in **over 200 languages**

### 3. Ask other professionals

Try your doctor, or your child's school nurse or guidance counselor.

### 4. Contact a therapy matching service

> Note: Mass General Hospital does not endorse any non-Mass General affiliated programs.

- **Therapy Matcher** (social work) — 📞 [800-242-9794](tel:+18002429794) · [therapymatcher.org](https://therapymatcher.org)
- **William James INTERFACE Referral Service** — see if your community participates at [interface.williamjames.edu](https://interface.williamjames.edu), then call 📞 [888-244-6843](tel:+18882446843)
- **LifeStance** — call their intake department at 📞 [617-405-5735](tel:+16174055735) · [lifestance.com](https://lifestance.com)
- **Complete your own online search:**
    - **Thriveworks** — 📞 [628-266-4892](tel:+16282664892) · [thriveworks.com](https://thriveworks.com)
    - **Psychology Today Therapist Finder** — [psychologytoday.com/us/therapists](https://www.psychologytoday.com/us/therapists)

### 5. Speak with your Employee Assistance Program (EAP)

Your EAP may provide short-term counseling, help you identify longer-term needs, and refer you to a therapist.

### 6. Ask your friends

You may find that friends or family have had therapy themselves and can make trustworthy recommendations.

---

en.description: What mindfulness is, how it can help, three simple practices to try, and apps to support a daily habit — written for teens.

content.markdown:
Practicing mindfulness is a way to be present in your everyday life — whether you're at school, at home, or out with friends. Here you'll learn about mindfulness and how it can help you feel less stressed and live in the moment every day.

## What is mindfulness?

**Mindfulness** is being present and aware of the moment without judging your thoughts, feelings, and **body sensations** (what you feel physically). The past or future isn't on your mind. Instead, you are aware of how you feel and what you think here and now.

> **Did you know?** Mindfulness is not sitting still and doing nothing — but it can be if you want. Mindfulness is simply being aware of your thoughts, feelings, and surroundings, and not judging or getting wrapped up in them.

## How can mindfulness help me?

Mindfulness is helpful in many ways, including helping you:

- Do better in school
- Concentrate better in school and out of school
- Feel less stressed
- Sleep better at night
- Reduce pain in your body
- Cope with anxiety, depression, or other mental health issues
- Improve heart, stomach, and gut health

## How can I practice mindfulness?

The good thing about mindfulness is that you can do it **anywhere, any time**. You can even practice mindfulness around others and they would never know.

**Simply notice the sights, smells, and things that surround you.** Focus on what's there for you in the moment, right here, right now. If you find your mind starts to wander, that's okay. Find something in your surroundings to focus on that will bring you back to the here and now.

**Count your breaths, either aloud or in your head.** This is helpful if you're feeling stressed, nervous, or overwhelmed. Breathe in for 5 seconds, counting *1-2-3-4-5*. Breathe out for 5 seconds, counting *1-2-3-4-5*. Simply be aware of your stressed or nervous feelings. Don't judge those feelings or try to push them away — they will pass as you count and breathe.

**Release tension in your body.** Sit, stand, or lie down in a comfortable position. Simply notice where you feel tense or stressed. When you breathe in, picture yourself gathering the stress or worry into a cloud. When you breathe out, picture yourself releasing that stress or blowing the cloud away.

## Smartphone apps for mindfulness

There are many apps that can help you learn to practice and use mindfulness every day:

- **[Calm](https://www.calm.com)** — A meditation website and app designed to bring peace to your mind. Some content is free; longer programs are paid.
- **[MindShift CBT](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/mindshift-cbt/id634684825)** — A free app designed to teach you positive ways of coping with anxiety, stress, and feelings of being overwhelmed.

## A note for parents

Being mindful toward your teen, your friends and family, and your surroundings can help improve your own *and* your teen's mindfulness skills. Being mindful also includes being non-judgmental, kind, grateful, loving, patient, forgiving, trusting, open, generous, gentle, and curious.

---

*Revised August 2016. Created by Cate Medeiros, MGH Adolescent and Young Adult Medicine.*

en.description: How to model mindfulness for toddlers, two breathing exercises to practice together, and a quick S.T.O.P. technique for caregivers.

content.markdown:
Children and adults can benefit from practicing mindfulness — the process of pausing to bring attention to the present moment. Here you'll learn more about mindfulness, why it's important, and how you can start practicing mindfulness with your child on a regular basis.

## What is mindfulness?

**Mindfulness** is a way to purposefully pay more attention to our bodies, thoughts, and emotions. It helps your mind and body become more aware of the moment and create a feeling of inner calmness.

## Why is it important to teach mindfulness to young children?

Growing up can be very stressful starting from the moment you are born (picture a tired, hungry baby). Toddlers and preschoolers often struggle with self-control and language. Teaching mindfulness can give children and their caretakers a tool to decrease anxiety and improve patience for the rest of their lives.

The benefits of mindfulness include:

- Decreased stress and social anxiety
- Increased happiness, compassion (concern and caring for others), and empathy (the ability to understand and share the feelings of another)
- Improved attention, focus, and impulse control

## How do you practice mindfulness?

There are various ways to practice mindfulness: concentration, breathing exercises, thinking positively, and feeling and expressing gratitude.

### Start by practicing it yourself

- **Be fully present and engaged** when you are spending time with your child. Make eye contact. Don't look at your phone often when your child is around.
- **Treat other people kindly** even when you are feeling frustrated or upset.
- **Choose activities that involve focus, creativity, and curiosity** — such as reading or making art rather than watching TV.
- **Stay calm.** When your child gets upset, try not to become agitated.
- **Express gratitude** for what you are thankful for, and teach your child to do the same.

### Then try these tips with your toddler

- **Teach your child how to recognize their feelings** (both good and bad) and how to describe them through words or pictures.
- **Teach your child forgiveness.** If there is a problem, discuss it. Help your child understand the problem will get better. If a child misbehaves, make an effort to show that you forgive them.
- **Teach your child breathing exercises.** *(See below.)*

## What is mindful breathing?

As young children learn to manage strong emotions, deep breathing can be part of the process. Mindful breathing can help your child become more familiar with their body and its rhythms. You can practice it *in the moment* when your child is having trouble controlling their emotions (crying, frightened, screaming, hitting). You can also practice mindful breathing as part of your child's morning or bedtime routine. Practicing at times that are *not* stressful can make mindful breathing easier when tougher situations arise.

### Finger-Counting Breaths

A useful exercise to try anywhere to calm a child who is having a tantrum, or even just to take a moment to regroup. Do it together with your child.

1. Create gentle fists with your hands.
2. With each breath, take one finger out from your palm. For example, on your first exhale, open your right thumb from your fist. Pause and take a breath in.
3. On your next exhale, take out your right pointer finger. Pause and take a breath in.
4. Continue until all your fingers are uncurled.

### Deep Breaths Before Bed

Before bed, take a few minutes to calm your mind and body down with this exercise.

1. Take a deep breath in through the nose. As you breathe out, say *"three,"* but hold it out: *"threeee."*
2. Take another deep breath in. On the next breath out, say *"twoooo."*
3. Take a last deep breath in and let it out, saying *"one,"* but hold it out: *"onnee."*
4. Relax for a few more breaths and try to enjoy the feeling of calmness.
5. Repeat if desired.

## S.T.O.P. for parents and caregivers

This popular short exercise can be woven into your day anytime you are feeling stressed, upset, or out of touch with the present moment.

- **S — Stop.** Take a pause from what you are doing. Put things away for a minute.
- **T — Take a few deep breaths.** Feel the sensation of your own breathing. You can even say to yourself *"in"* and *"out"* as you inhale and exhale if it helps you concentrate.
- **O — Observe.** Take note of your thoughts, feelings, and emotions — good or bad. Name them and notice how they are affecting your body. What is your posture? Are you having aches or pains? Are you feeling worried?
- **P — Proceed.** If you can, do something that will support you in that moment (talk to a friend, have a cup of tea). Then continue what you were doing.

## Helpful resources for learning to practice mindfulness

- **[Mindfulness for Children](http://annakaharris.com/mindfulness-for-children)** by Annaka Harris — audio instructions on mindful awareness exercises.
- **[Peace Out](http://bedtime.fm/peaceout)** — daily audio short stories that help children calm down and relax through visualization and breathing exercises.
- **A Handful of Quiet: Happiness in Four Pebbles** by Thich Nhat Hanh — guide written by a Zen monk for parents who would like to introduce mindfulness and meditation into their homes.
- **[Resources for Teaching Mindfulness to Your Children](http://leftbrainbuddha.com/resources-for-teaching-mindfulness-to-your-children/)** by Sarah Rudell Beach — lists popular resources (posts, books, websites) for learning mindfulness.
- **Have You Filled a Bucket Today?** by Carol McCloud — a book that encourages children to see how easy it is to express love, kindness, and appreciation.
- **Mindful Games** by Greenland and Harris — a card deck of 55 mindfulness exercises for kids.
- **Sitting Still Like a Frog** by Eline Snel — exercises for helping children with anxiety, improved concentration, and handling emotions.
- **Sitting Together** by Sumi Loundon Kim — a comprehensive guide to mindfulness for the entire family, including a guide for parents, lesson plans for children, and an activity book.

---

*Sources: Adapted from "Three Ways for Children to Try Meditation at Home," Jillian Pransky, New York Times (5/10/16); and "Stressing Out? S.T.O.P." from mindful.org, Elisha Goldstein, PhD (August 2013).*

## Who can apply

Individuals **at least 16 years of age** who have had experience at Mass General Brigham for Children are invited to apply for membership on the council.

- Terms are **three years**
- Time and commitment levels vary depending on committee needs and candidate interests

## How to apply

In addition to the Family Advisory Council, the hospital offers a number of **standing committee opportunities** of varying time commitments for patients and families with specific interests.

## For adults

### Mass General Bereavement Support Group

Open to patients and employees of the Mass General community. An **8-week group** for people who have experienced the death of a loved one within the past 1½ years. The fee is covered by most insurances and Medicare.

For any questions, to refer, or to schedule a pre-group screening interview, contact the group leaders Ellen McCarthy, LICSW, or Carol McSheffrey, LICSW:

- 📞 [617-724-8021](tel:+16177248021)

### Association of Death Education & Counseling

Their website provides online resources for coping with loss. The organization can make referrals to support groups throughout the United States.

- 📞 [847-509-0403](tel:+18475090403)

### The Compassionate Friends

Organization dedicated to assisting families toward positive resolution of grief following the death of a child of any age, and to providing information to help others be supportive. Chapters located across the United States and internationally.

- 📞 [877-969-0010](tel:+18779690010)

### Hospice Foundation of America

Offers support and education about death, illness, and the process of bereavement — for those grieving personally or professionally. - 📞 [800-854-3402](tel:+18008543402)

A group for ages **5–18 and their parents** grieving the death of a parent or sibling. Meets 5:30 – 7:30 pm on the first Wednesday of October–June at Mass General Hospital. Organized by Mass General for Children, Child Life Services, and the Social Work Department.

Developed for children and teens (**6–15 years**) who share similar experiences with grief. The camp provides an educational, therapeutic experience that is also enjoyable, helping to counter the sense of isolation that can follow losing a loved one. Activities like swimming, focused arts and crafts, and small discussion groups help children and teens explore their thoughts and feelings about grief.

- 📞 [508-973-3426](tel:+15089733426)

title: Who’s Who on the PICU Team

en.description: A guide to every role on your child's PICU care team, what they do, and how they support your family.

content.markdown:
**Physicians (MD):** 

The Physicians on the unit consist of Attendings, Fellows, Residents, and Medical Students. Please see the “Critical Care Doctors” link on the app to learn more about the different roles of the medical team. 

 ---

**Nurses (RN):** 

The RNs on the PICU work 12-hour shifts, either from 7a-7p or 7p-7a. Your child’s Nursing Team provides high-level clinical care while managing the unique physical, emotional, and developmental needs of patients, often acting as a bridge between physicians, patients, and families. 

  ---

**Patient Care Assistants (PCA):** 

The PCAs on the PICU work in 4-, 8-, or 12-hour increments, both day and night. PCAs provide around-the-clock care to patients under the supervision of a nurse. 

  ---

**Respiratory Therapists (RT):** 

RTs evaluate, treat, and care for patients with breathing or cardiopulmonary disorders, ranging from asthma to chronic lung diseases and emergency trauma. There is an RT present on the PICU 24 hours a day. 

  ---

**Child Life Specialist (CLS):** 

CLS’s are trained to work with children in medical settings, using play and developmental interventions to help children and families adjust to, and understand, their experience in the hospital. 

  ---

**Art Therapy:** 

Art therapy uses simple art activities to help patients express themselves and develop a sense of well-being through the creative process. You do not have to be an artist to enjoy and take advantage of art’s powers to enhance wellness. 

  ---

**Music Therapy:** 

Music therapy can help support a child’s experience through active music making, gentle live music for relaxation, music-supported meditation, and much more. 

  ---

**Pet Therapy:** 

Specially trained dogs who visit your hospital room to help children cope and overcome the stress that they may experience during their stay. Ask your Child Life Specialist about our pet therapy schedule. 

  ---

**Social Work (SW):** 

SW is available to discuss new diagnoses as well as the crisis of hospitalization and family adjustment to hospitalization. SW can help support your child and family throughout the entire hospital stay. 

  ---

**Case Management (CM):** 

To ensure that patients are receiving the services they need to achieve an optimum quality of life, the CM coordinates treatments and providers, facilitates safe transitions between hospital and outpatient settings and educates patients, families and providers on best health practices and services in the outpatient setting. 
 
 ---

**Spiritual Care (SC):** 

As partners in healing, SC Providers serve patients, families, visitors and staff through comfort, encouragement and prayer. They embrace life-long learning, respect the dignity and worth of every person, and honor the sacredness of the human spirit. SC services are always free, private and confidential. 

  ---

**Physical Therapy (PT):** 

Specialize in focusing on the large motor groups that contribute to walking, reaching, standing, and many more physical activities. 

  ---

**Occupational Therapy (OT):** 

Offer skilled treatment to help individuals achieve independence in all facets of their lives. OT facilitates early mobility, sensory regulation, and developmental support to improve recovery. 

  ---

**Speech-Language Pathologists (SLP):** 

Assess, diagnose, treat, and help to prevent communication and swallowing disorders in patients. 

  ---

**Nutritionists/Dieticians:** 

Trained to care for children with a variety of feeding difficulties. Nutritionists work together with the Dietary team to provide tailored nutritional care that helps support growth, development, and health management.
